At 10% progress, prioritize **baseline-initialized residual gating**: a small, controlled NextItNet modification whose effectiveness remains unverified.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Broad similarity crowds out specific recent matches; adaptive feature modulation could improve contextual discrimination. (2) Seasonal and already-satisfied purchases are extended into continuing demand; retaining the skip pathway permits selective updates without mandatory forgetting. Neither observation supplies compatibility or unmet-need labels. (3) Electronics has 10.04% negative-over-positive training positions and margin p10 −0.0106, motivating better discrimination without treating margins as validation accuracy. (4) History deletion generally harms measured rankings, arguing against indiscriminate cropping; exported-predictor parity remains unverified.

**Related-work insights.** (1) [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) supplies causal dilated residual transformations, making local gates a compatible extension. (2) [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) motivates carefully initialized residual modulation, although the proposed gate preserves the baseline update rather than initializing an identity block. (3) [PSL](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/db1d5c63576587fc1d40d33a75190c71-Abstract-Conference.html) cautions against aggressive exponential negative weighting; [TSSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07623) motivates semantic alignment but does not establish benefits from scratch under these constraints.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** Directions separate context transformation, ranking supervision, and permitted semantic evidence. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive and a limitation.

| Candidate | Scores | Assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Residual gate | 3/6/7/6/3 | O: localized adaptation, established gating; P: reusable mechanism, may become static; U: targets specificity and stale demand, cannot infer unmet needs; M: adapts discriminative features, separation gain unproven; D: small module, export coordination required. |
| Stochastic semi-hard negatives | 3/6/5/8/5 | O: controlled combination, established mining; P: improves learning signal, false negatives remain; U: challenges weak alternatives, lacks explicit recency conditioning; M: targets weak separation, training margins may mislead; D: bounded pools, exclusions add complexity. |
| Gated title encoder | 4/6/7/5/7 | O: constrained fusion, established alignment; P: adds specific evidence, sparse text limits learning; U: supports artist/task specificity, compatibility remains uncertain; M: enriches features, semantic clustering may worsen; D: standard layers, tokenization and deployment expand scope. |

**Selected algorithm.** For each completed causal residual update u, compute `g = sigmoid(W·concat(h,u)+b)/sigmoid(2)` and return `mask*(h+g*u)`. Initialize W=0, b=2. This starts at the supplied baseline and permits suppression or modest amplification. It explicitly targets broad-over-specific ranking and stale-demand persistence, while testing whether adaptive transformations reduce Electronics’ weak separation.

Keep the original loss, optimizer, dilation schedule and checkpoint rule. Train one network per category; preserve all fixed seeds, splits, limits and routing. Select exclusively by host macro validation HR@10. Verify causality, padding and exported score parity; retain diagnostic interfaces and measured definitions. Gates are neither intent measurements nor evidence of compatibility. No gain is claimed.

idea.description: Add a jointly trained positionwise, channelwise normalized sigmoid gate to each residual block of the corrected NextItNet. Preserve the causal convolutional backbone, dilation schedule, residual skip pathway and single scoring head. Initialize each gate so the initial network computes the original residual update.
idea.motivation: The proposal targets two reported user-facing failures: broad thematic matches displacing specific recent choices, and past purchases being extended into continuing demand. Conditioning update strength on the current hidden state and its proposed transformation may help the model distinguish contextually useful features. Electronics’ 10.04% sampled training wrong-rank rate and −0.0106 margin p10 provide a model-facing discrimination target. These observations motivate the experiment but do not establish that gating resolves either failure. Compatibility, ownership sufficiency and purchase need remain unobserved.
idea.implementation_notes:
Implement a Linear(2D,D) gate per existing residual block, with weight zero and bias 2. Compute the denominator using the same dtype/device sigmoid operation as the numerator. Apply the gate to the completed baseline residual update, including its existing dropout placement, immediately before residual addition. Preserve all baseline channel-only normalization and intermediate padding masks; zero padding after residual addition and keep embedding row zero fixed. Gate inputs at position t must contain only causal features available at t. The multiplier lies between zero and approximately 1.1353, so describe it as modulation rather than suppression alone. Retain the baseline objective, optimizer, batching, regularization and validation/checkpoint schedule to isolate this architecture change. Baseline equivalence holds at initialization with matching underlying parameters and stochastic realizations; it does not guarantee the same training trajectory.

Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; single-GPU execution; and trial-local artifacts. Train exactly one independent network per category, with no independent auxiliary scorers, score fusion or checkpoint averaging. Preserve the supplied splits and evaluator. Count training, diagnostics and failures against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; do not infer available remaining budget from the supplied history.

Read the maximum position with a nonzero item ID, never count−1, and preserve the baseline empty-history fallback. Save gate configuration and architecture version with each selected checkpoint. Update the embedded predictor writer with identical block definitions; load exactly one checkpoint per category. Verify evaluation-mode feature and candidate-score parity after reconstruction, with explicit category routes and eligible prefixes. No complete baseline source was supplied in this prompt, so this is an integration specification rather than an invented replacement train.py.

Keep family-specific sample_batch, ModelView, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return measured metrics and metric_definitions; diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must use both. Preserve the (None, sequence, positive, negative), B×L loader contract and view.model as the trained nn.Module. Fix manifest serialization without relying on inspectable dynamic class source; record explicit configuration and state metadata. Treat parity as unavailable until actually verified.

Report category results and supported qualitative findings separately; training-prefix sensitivity is in-sample dependence, not evidence of user preferences or validation gains. idea.pseudocode:
class ResidualGate(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, width):
        super().__init__()
        self.proj = nn.Linear(2 * width, width)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.proj.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(self.proj.bias, 2.0)

    def forward(self, h, completed_update, mask):
        logits = self.proj(torch.cat([h, completed_update], dim=-1))
        denominator = torch.sigmoid(logits.new_tensor(2.0))
        gate = torch.sigmoid(logits) / denominator
        return (h + gate * completed_update) * mask

originality.positive: A precise baseline-preserving initialization enables a focused adaptation of residual gating to the supplied NextItNet.
originality.negative: Residual gating is established; this is a task-specific architectural experiment rather than a new general mechanism.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled comparison could motivate further study of context-dependent residual transformations while preserving a single causal network.
future_potential.negative: Gates may become static or exploit score scale, and sampled validation gains would not establish improved full-catalog relevance or unmet-need reasoning.

code_difficulty.positive: The change uses one standard linear projection per block and leaves batching, loss and backbone topology intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct integration still requires padding discipline, architecture serialization, predictor-writer updates and verified deployment parity.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Provides the causal dilated residual convolutional backbone retained by the proposal.
limitations: Does not establish benefits for the proposed normalized residual gates on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: ReZero
contributions: Motivates careful initialization of residual modulation.
limitations: Its zero-initialized residual scaling differs from preserving a baseline residual update with a normalized sigmoid multiplier.

related_work.title: PSL
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies false-negative sensitivity from exponential weighting and alternative pairwise activations.
limitations: Provides motivation for an alternative objective experiment, not evidence that residual gating improves HR@10.

related_work.title: TSSR
contributions: The supplied search summary describes item-level and user-level textual–collaborative alignment.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness for a randomly initialized text encoder integrated into the constrained NextItNet setting.
